detailed_rationale: [DATA] Q4 FY26 (qtr ended Mar-2026): revenue Rs.995cr (+2.1% YoY), PAT Rs.277.86cr (+5.7% YoY, -6% QoQ), EBITDA margin +90bps YoY to 35%. FY26 full year: revenue Rs.3,790cr (+2% YoY) -- one of the slowest topline prints in the branded-MNC-pharma peer set -- but PAT Rs.1,012cr (+10% YoY) and EBITDA margin +290bps to 34%, i.e. FY26 growth was almost entirely margin/cost-driven (pricing actions, field-force productivity, AI-led cost optimisation), not volume-driven. Final dividend Rs.57/share declared (high payout, consistent with GSK India's low-capex distribution/brand model). [DATA/ONE-OFF] Management and press coverage (Whalesbook) attribute roughly 3-3.5pp of Q4 FY26 topline drag to a contract-manufacturing-organisation (CMO) supply disruption, now stated as resolved entering FY27 -- this is the one clean one-off in the print; FY27 double-digit revenue-growth guidance leans partly on this low-base recovery, not purely structural re-acceleration. [DATA] NPPA issued a Rs.3.54cr demand notice (dated 24-Jun-2026) alleging overcharging on scheduled formulations; company is appealing and states no material financial impact -- immaterial in size (~0.03% of FY26 PAT) but another data point on ongoing NLEM/NPPA friction. [DATA/INFERENCE] NLEM price control is estimated (analyst commentary, not a primary GSK filing) to cover ~35-38% of the portfolio (Ceftum, T-Bact since Sep-2022 NLEM inclusion), a structural cap on blended organic growth that pricing/mix-shift (Shingrix, specialty/oncology) must keep offsetting. [DATA] Valuation is rich: market cap ~Rs.41,300-42,500cr, P/E ~38.6x (25-Jun-26) to ~40.8x (13-Jul-26), P/B ~18.4x, price Rs.2,415-2,456 (13/20-Jul-26 marks) -- richer on P/B than peer Abbott India (~12.6x) despite a similarly decelerating volume story, reflecting the market's premium for GSK's cash conversion, debt-free balance sheet and dividend reliability. [DATA] No USFDA 483/OAI/warning-letter found against GSK India's Nashik manufacturing site (tablets/creams/ointments, BSI AMR Kitemark-certified 2026) in searches to 21-Jul-2026 -- Nashik is a domestic-formulations plant, not a US-export/biologics site, so the FDA-tail-risk framework this desk applies to generics exporters (Dr Reddy's-style 483 escalation odds) has materially lower relevance here; absence of evidence is not proof of a clean ongoing record, just a lower-probability risk vector for this specific name. [DATA] Q1 FY27 (Apr-Jun 2026) results NOT yet reported as of PIT date (21-Jul-2026); trading window has been closed since 1-Jul-2026 pending results, reopening 48hrs post-announcement -- based on GSK India's historical cadence (prior Q1 prints landed early Aug), expected board meeting is likely early-Aug-2026 [INFERENCE, not confirmed]. My fundamental read independently lands on Hold anyway, not because I'd escalate above quant but because the fundamentals genuinely sit between the two triggers: [INFERENCE] the FY26 print (2% revenue growth, margin-led PAT growth, one-off CMO drag) is too weak and the valuation (P/E ~40x, P/B ~18x) too rich to justify a constructive re-rating case, but the debt-free balance sheet, ~34% EBITDA margin, reliable high dividend payout (Rs.57/share), resolved supply disruption, and absence of any known USFDA plant-risk give no fundamental trigger for a Sell either. summary: [DATA] GSK India's FY26 growth was margin-led (PAT +10%) not volume-led (revenue +2%), with a CMO-related one-off costing Q4 ~3-3.5pp of topline; NLEM price control still caps ~35-38% of the portfolio. FY27 double-digit-growth guidance is real but partly a low-base bounce. Valuation (P/E ~40x, P/B ~18x) already prices continued execution. Quant scores Hold/Hold with high coverage; no USFDA plant flag found. Recommendation: Hold.
positive_para: [DATA] FY26 PAT +10% YoY to Rs.1,012cr on EBITDA margin expansion of +290bps to 34% (Q4 alone +90bps to 35%), driven by pricing, field-force productivity and AI-led cost optimisation. The CMO supply disruption that dented Q4 FY26 topline by an estimated 3-3.5pp is stated resolved, clearing the runway for management's guided double-digit FY27 revenue growth. Balance sheet is debt-free/cash-rich with a high, dependable dividend (Rs.57/share final FY26), typical of the MNC-pharma cohort. No USFDA 483/OAI/warning-letter found against the Nashik plant (BSI AMR Kitemark-certified 2026), and the plant is domestic-formulations-focused so US-export FDA-tail risk is structurally lower here than for generics-exporter peers. Vaccine/specialty mix-shift (Shingrix, oncology) offers a growth lever largely outside NLEM price control.
negative_para: [DATA] FY26 revenue grew just 2% YoY -- the growth story is entirely margin-led, and margin expansion has a ceiling. NLEM price control is estimated to cover ~35-38% of the portfolio (Ceftum, T-Bact), a structural drag on blended organic growth that the company must keep out-running with mix-shift and price hikes elsewhere. [DATA] Q4 FY26 growth was flattered by the resolution narrative around a one-off CMO supply disruption -- FY27's double-digit guidance is not yet proven organic re-acceleration, it partly reflects a low base. NPPA issued a fresh Rs.3.54cr overcharging demand notice (24-Jun-2026, under appeal) -- immaterial in rupee terms but a reminder that pricing-authority friction on this portfolio is recurring, not one-time. Valuation is demanding: P/E ~40x / P/B ~18x against a company that just printed 2% revenue growth -- [INFERENCE] a back-of-envelope reverse-DCF (EPS proxy ~Rs.60-63 off FY26 PAT/~16.24cr shares, WACC assumption 11%, Gordon-growth single-stage) implies the market is pricing ~8% perpetual earnings/dividend growth, which is a demanding multi-year ask given the NLEM drag and thin new-launch pipeline typical of this MNC-pharma model. Q1 FY27 not yet out (pending, expected ~early-Aug-2026), so the FY27 double-digit thesis is unconfirmed by any actual quarter yet.
reverse_dcf_judgment: [INFERENCE] Rich-to-fair, leaning rich. Using EPS proxy ~Rs.60-63 (FY26 PAT Rs.1,012cr / ~16.24cr shares), price ~Rs.2,415-2,456, and a single-stage Gordon-growth back-solve at an assumed 11% cost of equity, the implied perpetual growth priced into the stock is ~8%. FY26 actually delivered only 2% revenue growth (margin-led 10% PAT growth); FY27 guidance is double-digit but partly a low-base CMO-recovery bounce, not yet confirmed by a reported quarter. Sustaining ~8% earnings growth in perpetuity against a portfolio that is ~35-38% NLEM-price-controlled requires continued mix-shift into vaccines/specialty -- plausible given Shingrix/oncology momentum, but not something the FY26 print alone supports. Verdict: current multiple (P/E ~40x, P/B ~18x) is pricing continued execution, not offering a margin of safety; not a valuation-driven Sell case (quant floor is Hold regardless), but no upgrade case either.
